title: DSWD flags bogus UPLIFT aid for students
summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood,…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Assistance.

The posts claim that the government is giving ₱2,000 to elementary students, ₱3,000 to junior high school students, ₱5,000 to senior high school students, and ₱8,000 to college students under the program.
DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said educational assistance is not part of UPLIFT.

“Paalala po natin sa ating mga kababayan na walang educational assistance sa ilalim po ng ating UPLIFT Assistance. Ito pong assistance na ito ay tulong maibsan ang epekto ng pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin (We remind our fellow Filipinos that there is no educational assistance under UPLIFT Assistance. This assistance is intended to help ease the impact of rising prices of goods),” Dumlao said.
The posts also direct users to registration links, which the DSWD said are unauthorized.
Dumlao said there is no need to register for UPLIFT because its beneficiaries have already been identified using the latest Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) data.

“Mangyaring huwag po i-click ang inyong mga makikitang link na nagsasabing maaari kayong magparehistro dahil scam po ito (Please do not click on links claiming that you can register because these are scams),” she added.
Qualified beneficiaries under Groups 2 and 3 of the UPLIFT program receive ₱2,000 per month until December.

UPLIFT Assistance is among the Marcos administration’s initiatives to help poor, near-poor, and low-income Filipinos cope with the economic impact of the energy emergency brought about by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
The public may verify information on UPLIFT Assistance and other DSWD programs through the Department’s official social media pages or the DSWD Online Grievance Portal.
